candidates.title: Confidence-Calibrated Inference Expansion for Evaluator-Guided Test-Time Reasoning
candidates.abstract: Evaluator-guided reasoning presents a local control problem at every step: trust the current answer, return a fallback, or spend more inference. We formulate this choice as a compute-aware three-action controller, scoring terminal actions by predicted answer success and expansion by a rollout-based continuation-success surrogate, with compute cost priced explicitly. A local action-gap analysis characterizes when score errors can change a decision, while an expected regret bound accounts for errors along the realized expansion path. Guided by this analysis, we learn and calibrate action-specific confidence estimates, with local uncertainty penalties for ambiguous decisions. On held-out width expansion and revision tasks, the controller improves observed utility over calibration-selected fixed policies while reducing normalized online compute by about 30% and 16%, respectively. Across four Qwen3-8B seeds, compute is lower than fitted Q in both settings, while utility differences are small and mixed. The results frame evaluator-guided reasoning as resource allocation under uncertainty, rather than a uniformly stronger reasoner.

candidates.title: Pruning-Aware Multi-Cluster Co-Inference for Large AI Models in AI-RANs
candidates.abstract: The increasing scale and computational demands of large artificial intelligence models (LAIMs) present significant challenges for efficient inference in resource-constrained distributed environments. In this paper, we propose a multi-cluster LAIM co-inference framework, where an edge server equipped with multiple graphics processing units (GPUs) coordinates multiple user clusters to execute inference tasks collaboratively. Within each cluster, devices capture data from diverse perspectives and employ lightweight on-device LAIMs to extract local features. These features are then transmitted to the edge server, where they are aggregated and fused to generate a more accurate inference outcome. To reveal the fundamental trade-off between model pruning and collaborative inference performance, we develop a theoretical framework that characterizes the impact of pruning ratios and device contributions using rate-distortion theory and partial information decomposition. Based on this analysis, we formulate a joint optimization problem that determines the model pruning ratio, the task scheduling strategy, the bandwidth allocation, and the transmission power, with the goal of minimizing the inference distortion while satisfying the constraints of latency, energy consumption, and server capacity. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms existing benchmark schemes, achieving superior inference accuracy and resource efficiency in multi-cluster edge intelligence networks.
candidates.reason: 複数ユーザクラスタとGPU搭載エッジサーバが協調して大規模AIモデルの推論を実行するマルチクラスタ協調推論フレームワークを提案し、枝刈り率と協調推論性能のトレードオフを理論的に特徴付けており、分散推論への直接貢献が要旨で確認できるためacceptとした。

candidates.title: CARET: Training-Free Test-Time Scaling for Repository-Level Code Completion
candidates.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) dominates repository-level code completion: it retrieves cross-file context (R), then decodes one greedy completion (G). Existing work mainly focuses on retrieval and stops there. We argue both stages can be improved together, with generation in particular gaining from test-time scaling. We present CARET, a training-free method. For R, CARET routes among retrieval contexts using the agreement among its own samples, cascading to an alternative context when the samples scatter. For G, it samples candidates over a cached prompt prefix, so the long retrieved context is encoded once rather than once per sample. It then selects the final completion by reverse-context likelihood: a correct completion makes the code after the cursor more probable, so the same model grades its own candidates by reading ahead. Across CrossCodeEval, RepoEval-Line, and RepoEval-API with six code models (1.1B to 7B, four families), CARET improves exact match in all 18 combinations by 10.8 points on average over greedy decoding and 5.3 over self-consistency@10. Token-level compute stays near 1.45 times one generation (measured wall-clock 1.3-2.9 times, growing with generator size). Improving retrieval and generation together yields more accurate code than improving retrieval alone, at a budget that stays close to a single pass.

candidates.title: Lost in a Few Heads: Diagnosing and Repairing Block Selection in Sparse Attention
candidates.abstract: Sparse attention models read a few blocks of keys for every query at a fixed budget and can lose much of their long-context retrieval accuracy at that budget. We ask where this loss is made. Using exact attention mass selection at the shipped budget as an oracle, we show that the selector under-ranks the needle rather than running out of budget. We find attention heads that miss the needle by running a calibration probe that teacher-forces the answer and reads two quantities in every head. The first is the needle attention that the selector forfeits, and the second is the share of the answer's log-probability that fixing the head's selection restores, integrated along the path from the shipped selector to full attention. Four checkpoints of the InfLLM-V2 family and NOSA-8B lose multi-key retrieval in the same three blind heads, which attend to the needle while a mean-pooled key summary dilutes its single decisive token. Full attention in those heads or a 4-bit scorer that keeps the shipped budget recovers most of the loss without training. On MiniCPM4.1-8B at 64K, either fix lifts multi-key retrieval accuracy from 54.1 to 97.5%, level with full attention in every head. In production serving engines, full attention in those heads keeps 84 to 89% of the time to first token (TTFT) that sparse attention saves at 32K to 128K context length. Beyond the InfLLM-V2 selector lineage, one unified rule flags attention heads above a threshold swept on each checkpoint until they close most of the gap to full attention on calibration prompts. A similar small set of blind attention heads carry the loss for the SeerAttention-R gates, NSA, and DashAttention, whereas many such heads exist in MoBA. On Qwen3-8B with the SeerAttention-R gates, full attention in 18 of 288 key-value heads lifts multi-key retrieval accuracy from 29.8 to 97.7%.
